name: NY-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans about 18 points Democratic, a large structural edge for the incumbent party
Latimer has raised roughly $682,000 while Cinquemani shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 97 percent
No public general-election polling exists, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: an 18-point Democratic district, an incumbent with a decisive fundraising advantage over an opponent with no visible financial operation, and markets pricing the race near 97 percent Democratic. With no polls or ratings suggesting competition, the wide Democratic margin stands.
model.watch: Any polling showing a single-digit race, or significant Republican outside spending entering the district, would be the main signal to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New York's 16th District is a strongly Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of about 18 points toward the party. Incumbent George Latimer is running for re-election and holds clear financial advantages, having raised roughly $682,000, while Republican Joseph Cinquemani shows no reported fundraising in available records. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and money gives Democrats a substantial structural edge.

Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 97 percent, and no race raters list the contest as competitive. No public general-election polling exists, so the outlook rests on fundamentals rather than survey data. Even allowing for that gap, the evidence points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being turnout in a low-profile contest unlikely to draw significant outside spending or attention.
